summary: New Zealand lets visa-waiver nationals (the US, UK, EU, Canada, Japan and around 60 others) visit for up to 3 months — 6 for British citizens — but they must first obtain an NZeTA and pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Australians enter freely, everyone else needs a Visitor Visa, and every traveller must complete the digital New Zealand Traveller Declaration before arrival.

fee.notes: NZD 17 request fee, plus the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) paid at the same time — about NZD 117 in total for most tourists. Apply only on the Immigration New Zealand website or official app.
Fee for most applicants applying from outside New Zealand, including the International Visitor Levy; immigration fees are reviewed periodically — check the current amount before applying.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your intended departure date from New Zealand.

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry requirement for tourists, but strongly recommended — visitors generally pay for healthcare, and only accident-related treatment is covered by the national ACC scheme.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-waiver travellers must hold a ticket out of New Zealand (or evidence of onward travel arrangements) — airlines check before boarding.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show NZD 1,000 per person per month of stay (NZD 400 per month if accommodation is already paid for).

declarations.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD)
declarations.submitWindow: Before departure for New Zealand (opens 24 hours before flights)
declarations.text: Every traveller must complete the free digital New Zealand Traveller Declaration (website or app) before arrival, covering customs and biosecurity questions. Have the confirmation ready when you land.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of NZD 10,000 or more (or foreign equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Biosecurity is taken extremely seriously: declare ALL food, plants, animal products and outdoor equipment — undeclared risk goods carry an instant NZD 400 fine.
Clean hiking boots, tents and sports gear before you fly — officers inspect and can treat or seize dirty equipment.
Duty-free allowance: 50 cigarettes, 4.5 litres of wine or beer plus 3 bottles of spirits per adult.

payments.text: Cards and contactless (paywave) are accepted almost everywhere; cash is rarely needed. Some smaller merchants add a small surcharge for contactless credit cards. Tipping is not expected.

safety.text: New Zealand is one of the safest countries in the world. The main hazards are natural: changeable alpine weather, strong currents on beaches and rivers, and occasional earthquakes — check conditions before hikes and follow official advice.

source.name: UK FCDO — New Zealand travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to March is summer — the best window for hiking, beaches and road trips. June to September brings ski season in Queenstown and the Southern Alps.

tips.text: Declare all food and clean your hiking boots, tent and outdoor gear before flying — New Zealand biosecurity officers inspect equipment, and undeclared risk items mean an instant NZD 400 fine.
Complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration online or in the NZTD app before you fly — it is required for everyone and only takes a few minutes. Never pay a third-party site for it.

Drive on the left, and don't underestimate travel times — many scenic routes are winding two-lane roads, some unsealed gravel. Rental companies report jet-lagged tourists as a major accident cause: rest before driving.
Budget for the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy on top of the NZD 17 NZeTA fee — it is charged in the same transaction and funds conservation and tourism infrastructure.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No visa, but they must request an NZeTA before boarding and pay the International Visitor Levy — about NZD 117 in total. Once granted, it is valid for 2 years and allows visits of up to 3 months.

faq.question: How much does the NZeTA really cost?
faq.answer: The NZeTA request fee is NZD 17, but almost all tourists also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) in the same transaction — so expect about NZD 117. Apply only via immigration.govt.nz or the official NZeTA app.

faq.question: Do Australians need an NZeTA or visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No. Australian citizens are exempt from both the visa and the NZeTA under the Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement — they can visit, live and work in New Zealand freely. Australian permanent residents (non-citizens), however, do need an NZeTA.

faq.question: What is the New Zealand Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: The NZTD is a free digital declaration every traveller must complete before arriving, at travellerdeclaration.govt.nz or in the NZTD app. It covers customs and biosecurity questions and replaces the old paper arrival card.

faq.question: How long can I stay in New Zealand as a visitor?
faq.answer: Visa-waiver visitors get up to 3 months per visit (6 months for British citizens), with a maximum of 6 months in any 12-month period. For longer stays, apply for a Visitor Visa, which can allow up to 9 months.
